cases.notes: Two competencies carried past the rubric's sufficiency floor by measured outcomes, and a third claimed without a figure. The happy path the edge cases are measured against.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a systems design decision you owned.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I owned the systems design for our checkout service last year. We sharded the write path by region and cut median latency from 900 milliseconds to 240.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What did it cost to build?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The design work took 6 weeks with 2 engineers. It was the tightest schedule I have worked to and we protected it by cutting scope early.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a production problem you handled.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: During one incident I bisected the deploy and found the regression in 20 minutes. I kept the channel updated so nobody had to ask me where we were.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: And afterwards?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Afterwards we rewrote the response runbook and pages dropped from 14 a week to 3. The on call rota was rewritten at the same time so the load was shared.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you approach code review?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I care about collaboration in review but I have no figures to point at. It is the part of the job I would most like to get better at.

evidence.quote_contains: I owned the systems design for our checkout service
During one incident I bisected the deploy
Afterwards we rewrote the response runbook
I care about collaboration in review

known_limitations: The first systems design span deliberately covers two sentences: evidence-1 attributes an adjacent measured outcome to the claim beside it, so the quote is longer than the sentence that named the competency.

variants.why: Fillers, restarts and hedges added without changing a single fact. A judgement that moves here is moving on delivery, not on content.

cases.notes: One competency evidenced once, which is below the rubric's floor of two; one met with admitted uncertainty, which is a gap rather than a low result; one never reached at all. Three different reasons for saying nothing, and they are not interchangeable.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a systems design decision.

turns.speaker: candidate

turns.speaker: interviewer

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Honestly I am not sure I have a strong incident example. I have shadowed the on call rota but I have not carried the pager myself yet.

turns.speaker: interviewer

cases.notes: A genuine numeric conflict: the same headcount over the same period, stated two ways. The pair is a clarification prompt and nothing here infers anything about the person.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How large was the team on that platform?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The platform team had 4 engineers for the whole project. We sat together and nobody joined or left while it ran.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Say a bit more about the shape of it.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: There were 9 engineers on the platform team throughout. That was the headcount from the first week to the last.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What did you own on it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I owned the systems design for the ingest path, and it handled 30 thousand events a second. That was the piece I was accountable for end to end.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How was it checked?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The design review for it ran over 2 sessions. Everybody who would carry the pager was in the room for both of them.

evidence.quote_contains: I owned the systems design for the ingest path
The design review for it ran over 2 sessions
The design review for it ran over 2 sessions

contradictions.why: Four engineers for the whole project and nine throughout the same project cannot both be the headcount.

known_limitations: One sentence naming two competencies produces a span for each. That is the reading the rules give, and both spans quote the same words.

cases.notes: Two different incidents, two different recovery times, and no conflict at all. evidence-1 pairs them because they share subject tokens and disagree numerically. The dataset records this as a false positive so the harness counts it rather than scoring it as a success.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about an incident you handled.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: During the incident response we restored the service in 45 minutes. Most of that was working out which change had done it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Did that get better?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The next incident response took 12 minutes because the runbook was ready. It was a completely separate fault, months later.

evidence.quote_contains: we restored the service in 45 minutes
took 12 minutes because the runbook was ready

contradictions.why: Two separate incidents recovered at different speeds. Improvement over time reads as a numeric disagreement to a rule that cannot tell one event from another.

known_limitations: This is the shape of contradiction false positive evidence-1 produces most: a measured improvement in one subject across two moments in time.

cases.notes: Word timing never arrived, so delivery cannot be measured. The content still can be, which is the distinction that matters: an unassessable delivery is not an unassessable answer, and neither is a low result.
